extracted.intended_audience: applicants, stakeholders, and the public participating in Federal Register notices and Department of Energy/agency proceedings
extracted.subtask_description: Procedural and substantive criteria found in Federal Register notices governing (a) environmental impact statement scoping and alternatives, (b) fellowship and grant application requirements, (c) DOE unsolicited awards and import authorization proceedings, (d) FACA meeting closure determinations, and (e) Office of Hearings and Appeals discovery/refund adjudications.

rubrics_metrics.name: EIS alternatives (must-identify alternatives)
rubrics_metrics.description: Alternatives for the proposed action must be identified and considered (examples given: A. No Action; B. Issuance of a Special Use permit on 84,000 acres and interchange of about 32,000 acres; C. Issuance of the Special Use permit with no change in current activities; D. Issuance of the Special Use permit with added activities including development of a tank task force maneuver area). For the land exchange action the No Action alternative would be retention and management by the Department of Army of the 16,000 acres, and other exchange-site alternatives should be considered.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The draft EIS should analyze each reasonable alternative. Alternatives should include the No Action alternative and other practicable options (e.g., partial permit issuance, full permit, permit with added activities, alternate land exchange sites).

rubrics_metrics.name: EIS scoping and public participation requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Agencies will conduct a scoping process to determine significant environmental issues; public scoping meetings will be held and dates announced later; notification will be by letter, public announcement, and news releases. Individuals, organizations, or governmental agencies are encouraged to participate in scoping.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Public participation should (1) help define the scope of the analysis; (2) identify significant environmental and social issues; (3) provide published and unpublished data; (4) provide personal knowledge of relevant issues; and (5) recommend mitigation measures. Information can be submitted by writing to listed points of contact or by attending scoping meetings. A Draft EIS is expected to be filed and available for public review by the stated date (here: August 1990).

rubrics_metrics.name: FACA meeting closure determination
rubrics_metrics.description: Meetings concerning matters listed in 5 U.S.C. 552b(c)(1) (e.g., classified program details) may be closed to the public in accordance with section 10(d) of Public Law No. 92-463, as amended (5 U.S.C. App. II 10(d)).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A determination must be made that the Advisory Group meeting concerns exempted matters under 5 U.S.C. 552b(c)(1) in order to close the meeting. Such determinations are announced in the Federal Register with citation to the statutory authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fellowship program eligibility and application requirements
rubrics_metrics.description: Program provides financial assistance through approved institutions to full-time students pursuing a graduate degree in areas related to programs for limited English proficient persons. Notices specify deadlines for transmittal, availability date for applications, available funds, estimated range and average of awards, estimated number of awards, project period, and applicable regulations (EDGAR and program-specific CFR parts).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must follow EDGAR (34 CFR part 85) and program regulations (34 CFR parts 500 and 562). Notices may identify an invitational priority (e.g., programs leading to a doctoral degree) but under 34 CFR 75.105(c)(1) such a priority does not confer competitive or absolute preference. Contact information and authoritative statutory citation (e.g., 20 U.S.C. 3323) are provided for further inquiries.

rubrics_metrics.name: NAEP Governing Board functions and record availability
rubrics_metrics.description: The Board advises the NCES Commissioner on policies to improve the National Assessment of Educational Progress; develops specifications for design, methodology, analysis and reporting; selects subject areas and objectives; and establishes standards and procedures for interstate and national comparisons. Records of proceedings are kept and available for public inspection at specified office hours and address.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Meeting notices must include date/location, agenda summary, statement of functions, and where records are available for inspection with office hours.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criteria for awarding DOE financial assistance based on unsolicited application (10 CFR 600.14)
rubrics_metrics.description: DOE may award financial assistance based on an unsolicited application if, after technical evaluation under 10 CFR 600.14(d) and (e), the project is meritorious, probability of achieving objectives is high, facilities and capabilities are appropriate, and key personnel qualifications are exceptional. Additional factors: regional infrastructure supporting the project, collaborative partners (e.g., labs, universities), innovative approach not eligible under existing solicitations, and the determination that a competitive solicitation would be inappropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Awards may be limited initially (e.g., one-year award with later years contingent on performance). Cost sharing and total estimated costs should be stated; distribution is subject to budget limitations and research results. Awarding authority should document the technical evaluation and the rationale for treating the proposal as unsuitable for competitive solicitation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Invitations and procedural requirements for protests, motions to intervene, and written comments in DOE import proceedings
rubrics_metrics.description: Notices invite protests, motions to intervene, notices of intervention and written comments. To be a party and have written comments considered as the basis for decisions, a person must file a motion to intervene or notice of intervention as applicable. Filing a protest alone does not make the protestant a party, though protests and comments from non-parties will be considered. All filings must comply with regulations in 10 CFR part 590.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Deadlines and filing addresses are specified (e.g., filings due by 4:30 p.m., e.s.t., February 5, 1990, to Office of Fuels Programs at named address). Docket copies of applications are made available in specified docket rooms during listed hours. Parties seeking to be heard should ensure procedural compliance with cited CFR provisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Burden and substance of comments in DOE gas import competitiveness determinations
rubrics_metrics.description: The DOE's gas import policy guidelines emphasize market competitiveness as the primary consideration in determining public interest. Applicants asserting competitiveness place a presumption; parties opposing the application bear the burden of overcoming that assertion and should comment on competitiveness as set forth in the policy guidelines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Opponents should address competitiveness directly and provide factual evidence/reasoning to rebut the applicant's competitiveness assertion per DOE policy (see 49 FR 6684, February 22, 1984).

rubrics_metrics.name: NEPA compliance for import/export authorizations (categorical exclusion presumption)
rubrics_metrics.description: DOE may rely on a categorical exclusion for approval/disapproval of an import/export authorization 'in cases not involving new construction,' as added to DOE NEPA guidelines. Application of the categorical exclusion raises a rebuttable presumption that the DOE's action is not a major Federal action under NEPA.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Unless DOE receives comments indicating the presumption should not apply in a particular case, no further NEPA review will be conducted. Commenters should specifically raise NEPA-related concerns to overcome the presumption.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standards for requesting additional procedures in DOE adjudications (oral presentation, conference, trial-type hearing)
rubrics_metrics.description: A party seeking additional procedures may request: additional written comments, an oral presentation, a conference, or a trial-type hearing. Requests must explain why the additional procedure is necessary. For oral presentations, identify the substantial question of fact, law, or policy, show that it is material and relevant, and demonstrate why an oral presentation is needed. Requests for conferences should show why the conference would materially advance the proceeding. Requests for trial-type hearings must show factual issues genuinely in dispute that are relevant and material and that a trial-type hearing is necessary for full disclosure of the facts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If additional procedures are scheduled, notice will be provided to all parties. If no party requests additional procedures, a final opinion and order may be issued based on the official record including application and responses pursuant to the notice, in accordance with 10 CFR Sec. 590.316.

rubrics_metrics.name: Standards for discovery in Office of Hearings and Appeals (relevance and appropriateness)
rubrics_metrics.description: Discovery motions are granted in part where requested information is relevant to disputed factual issues (e.g., credibility of a witness whose testimony is potentially biased). Discovery requests primarily concerning legal issues or ERA's legal contentions (as opposed to disputed facts) are usually inappropriate and may be denied.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OHA examines whether requested discovery bears on factual issues genuinely in dispute. Requests aimed at legal theories or ERA's contemporaneous regulatory construction are typically denied. Requests relevant to witness credibility (e.g., deals made for testimony) may be permitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: Criteria for issuance of protective orders
rubrics_metrics.description: Protective orders may be issued where parties stipulate and where DOE finds the stipulation appropriate (e.g., to allow sharing of confidential documents subject to protective terms).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A Stipulation of Protective Order signed by the parties and reviewed by DOE may be approved as a Protective Order; the notice summarizes the substance and the DOE's finding that issuance is appropriate.

rubrics_metrics.name: Refund application documentation and presumptions of injury
rubrics_metrics.description: Refund applicants must document the volume of purchases to support claims. Various presumptions of injury may apply: small claims injury presumption for claims $5,000 or less, presumptions for end-users/resellers/consignees, and consolidation of applications for entities under common ownership when combined allocable share exceeds thresholds. Applicants may elect to limit refunds (e.g., accept larger of $5,000 or 40% of allocable share, or limit refund to 41% of full volumetric amount), and OHA may accept applicants' alternative gallonage figures if supported by their actual records.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Successful refunds depend on adequate documentation of purchase volumes and correct application of presumptions. Where applicants are indirect purchasers or resellers with small allocable shares, presumptions simplify awards. Applicants choosing to limit their recovery must follow prescribed election options. OHA will evaluate and may accept applicant-supplied records over company records when justified.
